chunks: And with this chain, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, the most unjust of people to Allah, the Exalted, is one who kills someone other than his murderer, and one who strikes someone who did not strike him.'
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be 'most unjust' to Allah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to define 'aqqa' (extreme ingratitude or injustice) not merely as neglect, but as active, unprovoked aggression against the innocent. This hadith establishes a foundational principle in Shia jurisprudence and ethics, distinguishing between justified retaliation (qisas) and unjustified aggression, thereby emphasizing that violating the sanctity of life without cause is a direct affront to Allah's decree.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 7.  Imam  Ja’far  Sadiq  (a.s.)  said,  “A  person most unjust  in Allah’s eyes is one who kills a person who hasn’t murdered him or hurt one who did not hurt him.”
